sources.citation: Ruk Sindhi. 2025. Baluchistan: Historical Homeland of Sindhis. English edition. Karachi. Chapter 15 'Dialects of Sindhi Language in Balochistan' (section 'Jadgali Dialect') and chapter 11 'Sindhi Jadgal of Iran'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: no phonology content for Jadgali: etymology Jad(Jat)+gal ('Jat-speaking'), distribution (Gwadar, Makran, Bela, Panjgur; Iranian Balochistan; Oman), 1998 census 100,000, closeness to Lasi. The only sound remarks in the chapter concern Lasi (softening of some Sindhi consonants), quoted from N. B. Khan Baloch.

sources.citation: Nourzaei, Maryam. 2024. Kholosi. In Haig et al. (eds.), Post-predicate elements in the Western Asian Transition Zone, 175-195. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14266341
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Jadgali stress; Jadgali is mentioned only as the other Indo-Aryan outlier in Iran (location, no contact with Kholosi, retains split ergativity). Describes Kholosi (khol1240), not Jadgali.

sources.citation: ELAR deposit: Nourzaei, Maryam. 2023. Documentation of the Jadgali language. Endangered Languages Archive, hdl:2196/m90p1784-6090-2r4m-861n-e5o46432717n
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept

sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: nothing: classification/name record only; ALI holds no language-data document (lexical or phonological questionnaire) and no bibliography entry linked to Jadgali (link-references view returns only the classification map). Logged so later passes do not re-mine ALI for Jadgali.

sources.citation: Brohi, Dad Muhammad 'Khadim'. 2012. بلوچستان ۾ سنڌي ٻوليءَ ۽ ادب جو اڀياس [Balochistan mein Sindhi boli'a ain adab jo abhyas / A study of Sindhi language and literature in Balochistan]. (Published PhD thesis, supervisor Abdul Jabbar Junejo.) Hyderabad: Sindhi Language Authority. ISBN 978-969-9098-37-6. In Sindhi. Online edition in the SLA Sindhi Virtual Library (book 57; chapters read/1391-1402).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Treats Jadgali as one of c. 12-14 regional dialects (muhavira) of Sindhi; gives its territory ('هوڏانهن مڪران خطي جي جدگالي محاوري جي حدن ۾ ارماڙي ۽ گوادري ٻوليون به ننڍن محاورن جي حيثيت رکن ٿيون' = 'within the Jadgali dialect of the Makran region the Ormara and Gwadar varieties also rank as sub-dialects'), a Jadgali column in comparative word tables (e.g. جنجير / ڪاغذ / جتيم / ڪوشيس / آزات / گوڙو / با / ڦوٽو) and notes on letters/sounds shared with Lasi, Kohistani, Firaqi, Khetrani. No statement on word stress, accent placement or tone; the only 'Tone (ٽون) / accent' sentence in the chapter…

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic table rows only (alternate names, location, speaker figure from Ethnologue; literacy materials attributed to Baloch 2003; domains/vitality 'Not known'). Nothing on phonology, stress or tone.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. 1919. Linguistic Survey of India VIII.1 (Sindhi and Lahnda) [local djvu text ]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only an identity remark: in Baluchistan Lahnda and Sindhi are called 'Jatki' or, by the Baloch, 'Jadgali'/'Jagdali'; no description of the Makran Jadgali variety and nothing on its stress.

sources.citation: Hughes-Buller, R. 1906. Baluchistan District Gazetteer Series, vol. VII: Makran. Bombay: Times Press. Chapter 'Population', section 'Language', p. 77.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: no phonology content: one paragraph - three languages in Makran (Baluchi, Jadgali, Lori-Chini); 'Jadgali is spoken by the few Jadgals of Kulanch and is practically identical with Lasi, the language of Las Bela, and an offshoot of Sindi'; remarks on its survival amid Balochi. Nothing on sounds, stress or tone.

sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: classification (Indo-European > Indo-Iranian > Indo-Aryan > NW, Sindhi), location, speaker numbers, 'considered a dialect of Sindhi', speakers mostly literate in Sindhi, distinct from the Jat languages of Ukraine/Afghanistan.
